# Incident Report: Malware Infection via Fake FedEx Tracking Lure

**Evidence:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, 1962-second capture). No IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory — all findings below are derived directly from packet analysis.

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| Logged-in user account | **plucero** (full name decoded from Kerberos/LDAP traffic: Pierce Lucero) |
| Domain | lafontainebleu.org (DC: WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org, 10.8.15.4) |

Confirmed via ARP (IP↔MAC), NBNS name registration, DHCP hostname option, and Kerberos `CNameString` (`DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` and `plucero`).

## Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no Suricata/IDS export was provided in the evidence set).

The infection chain and C2 behavior match the profile of the **Matanbuchus loader**:
- Delivery via a fake package-tracking/invoice lure hosted behind Cloudflare.
- A ZIP archive containing a single, heavily padded `.js` file (~7 MB of junk filler text wrapping a small amount of functional JScript) — a known Matanbuchus obfuscation technique to defeat size-based AV scanning.
- The downloader retrieves a second-stage PE32+ DLL from a bare IP address over HTTP using **Microsoft BITS** (`bitsadmin`/BITS jobs, User-Agent `Microsoft BITS/7.8`), served with `Content-Type: text/html` to disguise the binary — another Matanbuchus hallmark.
- Post-infection, the host beacons continuously to the same bare-IP host on port 80 using `GET /` and `POST /` with a large encrypted value in the `Cookie` header and encrypted binary request bodies — an HTTP-based C2/exfiltration channel consistent with Matanbuchus's loader/backdoor traffic.

## Timeline

| Rel. time | Event |
|---|---|
| t=74.7s | GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (104.21.55.70) returns a ZIP disguised as `application/octet-stream` |
| t=135.9–136.9s | BITS `HEAD`/`GET` of `/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` from 72.5.43.29 — delivers PE32+ DLL payload |
| t=196.8s → end of capture (t≈1962s) | Continuous encrypted HTTP GET/POST beaconing to 72.5.43.29:80 (400+ TCP sessions) |

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — bare-IP HTTP C2/beaconing host, User-Agent spoofed as `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`; also served the second-stage payload over BITS.

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolved to 104.21.55.70, Cloudflare-fronted) — served the initial malicious ZIP.
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — referenced inside the downloader JS as part of the same fake-FedEx lure infrastructure (queried by the host per DNS log; associated URL string embedded in the JS padding: `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?...`).

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://104.21.55.70/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` (Host: quote.checkfedexexp.com) — delivered the ZIP.
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS download of the second-stage DLL.
- `http://72.5.43.29/` — repeated GET/POST C2 beacon endpoint.

**Transferred files and hashes**

| File | Type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| `managements?...` (ZIP, from quote.checkfedexexp.com) | ZIP archive | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside the ZIP) | Padded JScript downloader (~6.99 MB) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (from 72.5.43.29, via BITS) | PE32+ DLL, x86-64, GUI subsystem | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` |

**Note on the BITS traffic to `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` / `199.232.210.172` and OCSP/NCSI/MSN/Bing/Office/Kerberos/LDAP traffic:** this is legitimate Windows Delivery Optimization, connectivity-check, and domain-joined workstation background traffic — benign context, not an indicator.

**Not grounded / not observed:** no DNS resolution record was captured tying `72.5.43.29` to any of the `checkfedexexp.com` hostnames; it is treated here strictly as an IP-literal C2/staging host reached directly by the malware, not as a resolved domain.
